_meta.name: Video analysis: 'Five things to remember if you want to build reliable apps' (dark-mode 3D-UI explainer reel)
_meta.purpose: Structured description of the reference video 'Claude_Code_Reel2.mp4' so it can be understood in a later conversation without re-uploading it. Covers format, brand/visual language, motion language, persistent HUD, a beat-by-beat timeline with captions and visuals, and reusable components.
_meta.how_derived: Frames sampled at 1 fps (94 frames) and inspected visually; captions read from frames. Audio track exists (voiceover) but was NOT transcribed - captions are assumed to mirror the voiceover. Timestamps are +/-1s; sub-second animation timing is inferred.
_meta.important_note: This video is NOT the 53.7s light-theme 'YouTube Agent Skill' reel described by the previously supplied reel-style-spec JSON. It shares the same genre (centered-headline, one-hero-object, glossy 3D UI cards, italic-serif accent words, blur-swap captions, no avatar) but is 93.75s, DARK themed, and teaches a numbered 5-point list with a progress HUD. Treat it as a sibling style ('reel 3 / dark numbered explainer').
_meta.caveat: Hex values are eyeballed from compressed frames - approximate.

format.audio: Voiceover (not transcribed). Each caption chunk = one spoken phrase, roughly 0.7-1.5s per chunk; words appear as spoken.

context.topic: Five principles for building reliable apps (aimed at beginners / vibe-coders building with AI).
context.title_line: Five things to remember if you want to build reliable apps.
context.format_type: Numbered listicle explainer. Intro hook (0-4s) -> 5 numbered sections -> CTA.
context.audience: Non-expert app builders; concrete everyday examples (subscription billing, payments/email/AI APIs, document access, customer bug report, deploys).
context.cta: Grab the 'Reliable app checklist' from the link in bio and follow for more.

recurring_example_data.user: Ryan, id U-104, Pro plan $12/month, next renewal Dec 1

five_points.label: Data
five_points.lesson: Structure data so users, subscriptions and payments are linked, and use database transactions so related changes succeed or fail together.

five_points.label: APIs
five_points.lesson: Work with APIs defensively: set timeouts, handle errors, and keep unaffected features working when one service is down.

five_points.label: Access
five_points.lesson: Access control: a login isn't enough. The server must check permissions on every request; hiding a button doesn't protect what's behind it.

five_points.label: Debugging
five_points.lesson: Find the failed step using logs and error tracking (with a request id) instead of guessing fixes.

five_points.label: Deploy
five_points.lesson: Deploy changes safely: test in a separate environment, manage config and secrets, be ready to roll back; but code rollback does not equal data restore for database changes.

brand.style_name: Dark glossy 3D-UI explainer (neon indigo on near-black navy)

colors.bg_glow_indigo_violet: #1A1740 to #2A1F55 (soft radial glow bottom-center / bottom-right, brightens on emphasis beats)
colors.grid_lines: very faint blue grid in perspective on the floor, fading upward
colors.accent_indigo_blue: #6F8AF5 (primary accent; italic serif accent words, buttons, active steps, big numerals)
colors.accent_violet: #A78BFA / #B79CF5 (secondary, lavender tiles, 'owner', AI orb, plan_id highlight)
colors.card_dark: #101830 (dark navy cards/panels with subtle lighter border)

brand.color_roles: Indigo/blue = default accent for 'good/primary/active' and for the italic serif key word. Green = success/valid/allowed. Coral/red = failure, danger, missing, denied. Violet/lavender = secondary tiles (owner, AI, v2, user avatars). Orange/peach used sparingly as small status dots and one DB row. White only for headline text, receipt and documents.

fonts.headline_sans: Inter-style bold grotesk, weight 700-800, white, ~52-60px at 1080w, centered
fonts.headline_accent_serif: Italic high-contrast serif (Instrument Serif / Playfair Italic style) in accent indigo, same size as sans, ONE per chunk (reliable, data, transactions, APIs, requests, or neither, permissions, why, failed step, safely, data restore, Reliable (checklist title))
fonts.mono: JetBrains Mono-style for ids/paths/log lines/timers (U-104, S-208, P-312, R-218, GET /documents/105, '2.1s', 'REGION eu-west')
fonts.big_numerals: Heavy extruded 3D numerals '01'-'05' in glossy indigo-to-violet gradient with thick bevel/shadow

layout._note: Percentages of the 9:16 frame. Same skeleton every beat.

progress_hud.position: top-center, y about 5.5%, small pill ~370px wide
progress_hud.content: mono step number + label on the left (e.g. '01 Data', '02 APIs', '03 Access', '04 Debugging', '05 Deploy') and 5 small dash segments on the right; segments up to the current step are lit indigo, the current one longer/brighter
progress_hud.visibility: Absent during the intro (0-3s). Appears at 4s with 'Number one'. During number-intro beats (e.g. 53-54s, 70-71s) the label cross-fades from the previous section to the new one. Stays through the CTA ('05 Deploy' with all 5 dashes lit).

headline.y_pct_center: about 8-10% when HUD present (line 1 at ~9%); 2-3 lines allowed, line wraps grow downward
headline.reveal: word-by-word as spoken; each new word fades/rises a few px. Latest word often briefly rendered in muted grey before turning white (see ghosted words 'want', 'database', 'subscription...', 'wait', 'more!').
headline.chunking: Short phrases that extend in place ('Five things' -> '...to remember' -> '...if you want' -> '...to build reliable apps.'). When a sentence ends, the old text blur-fades while the new chunk starts (ghosted old line visible for ~8 frames).
headline.accent_rule: Accent word(s) become italic serif in indigo, usually the key concept of the sentence.

hero_zone.note: One hero object/scene at a time, centered around 40-55% of height. Width 80-90% for cards, ~25-40% for icon objects (database, document stack, phone, envelope). Lots of empty dark space below the hero.

layers: near-black navy base gradient (top #050A17 to bottom #0A0F1F)
faint perspective grid on the floor (lines, low opacity), more visible in lower half
soft indigo/violet radial glow bottom-center, drifts slowly; becomes stronger on warning/emphasis beats (e.g. reddish tint around 26-28s API timeout, 43-46s Missing check, 64-66s failure)
tiny dust particles / dots, very low opacity
background.motion: glow drifts slowly; grid static. Hero objects cast soft colored glows onto the floor.

motion._note: Spring / ease-out only. Objects behave like soft glossy toys: pop with overshoot, tilt slightly, settle.
motion.enter: Cards: slide up ~40-60px + scale .94->1 + fade (spring). Tiles/icons: pop scale 0->1.1->1. Documents: fan out with slight rotation.
motion.exit: Blur-fade (blur 0->10px, opacity->0, scale .97) as the next headline chunk starts. Objects sometimes persist and transform (database persists from intro through section 1; the phone UI persists through section 2; document stack persists through section 3).
motion.big_numeral_beat: At the start of each section a giant 3D '0N' numeral pops in behind/below the hero while the headline says 'Number N is...'. It then drops back / shrinks away as the hero takes over.
motion.chip_pop: Small status chips ('Active', 'Committed', 'Allowed', 'Received', 'Saved', 'Both restored') pop with overshoot beside their object.
motion.cursor: White macOS arrow cursor glides to a target and clicks (Cancel subscription at 7s, a spinner/button at 26s, doc ID field at 43s, 'Roll back' at 83s, CTA button at 92-93s). Click = subtle ripple/hover highlight.
motion.typing_and_fields: Sign-in form types 'alex' / 'alex@example.com' / masked password; URL path digits swap ('/documents/104' -> '/documents/105') with highlighted digits.
motion.spinners_timers: Ring spinners on loading rows; a countdown timer chip counts up in mono (1.0s -> 4.9s) with a circular dial whose needle sweeps and turns red at the 5s timeout.
motion.connectors: Thin curved or dotted lines connect objects (app->server, user->subscription->payment, comment->reply). Dotted line draws on with a moving dot.
motion.ring_pulse: Thin outline ring expands from an element on reveal beats (e.g. the red 'plan' pin, the envelope with 503).
motion.selection_boxes: Dashed coral/indigo rounded rectangle around the object in focus (API orb 2s, unavailable service 28-36s). Corner-bracket frame around transaction rows (17-19s).
motion.section_transition: Previous hero blur-fades while the HUD label cross-fades and the next big numeral rises. No hard cuts, no whip pans.
motion.emphasis_text: Large bold lower-third statements pop in under or over the hero: 'Together, or neither.' (19s, 'or neither' in italic serif), 'Find the failed step.' (67s), 'Code rollback != data restore' pill (88-89s).

scene_grammar.beat_template: [HUD pill] + [centered 1-3 line headline chunk with 1 italic-serif accent] + [one hero object or state change] + [optional chip/badge/emphasis line]. Heroes persist across several chunks and change state (data cards update, spinner turns to check, etc.).
scene_grammar.section_template: 1) big 3D numeral 'Number N is <topic>' (2-4s) -> 2) concrete failure story with a believable mini-UI -> 3) the rule stated plainly in the headline -> 4) visual resolution (green check / safe state) or emphasized takeaway line.
scene_grammar.pacing: Fast: new headline chunk about every 1s; sections of ~14-22s each; hero persists 2-5 chunks.
scene_grammar.narrative_pattern: Problem story first (something silently goes wrong: charged after cancel, API stalls app, someone edits an ID, customer says 'it's not working', rollback leaves bad data) then the principle.

caption_rules.style: Sentence case, no emoji, no stroke, no background box (except the 'Code rollback != data restore' emphasis pill and a few emphasis lines).
caption_rules.length: 2-8 words per visible chunk (chunks grow in place up to a full sentence of ~10 words over 3 lines).
caption_rules.voiceover_sync: Words appear on the frame spoken (+/-2 frames); newest word may show muted grey for a few frames before turning white.
caption_rules.accent: Max one italic serif indigo word/phrase per sentence. Used for: reliable, data, disagree, transactions, or neither, APIs, requests, permissions, why, failed step, safely, data restore, Reliable (checklist title).

do: Keep the dark navy background with faint floor grid and indigo/violet glow
Show each lesson as a tiny believable product scenario built from UI cards (subscription card, shop phone, request bar, logs, release box)
Show failure first (red/coral) then the fix (green/indigo)
Keep the persistent '0N Label' progress HUD at top during sections
Use a giant extruded 3D numeral to open each numbered section
Reuse hero objects by shrinking/relocating (database, phone, document stack, v2 box)
Use one italic serif accent word per sentence in indigo
dont: No presenter avatar or talking head
No hard cuts or whip pans
Don't show two large hero objects at once except during a blur-out
Don't introduce extra accent colours beyond indigo/violet + green (success) + coral (error) + a touch of peach
Don't use real brand logos or real people; all data (Ryan, Alex, Sam) is fictional

structure: Root: <AbsoluteFill> Background (gradient + grid + glow + particles) -> persistent ProgressHUD -> persistent Headline -> per-beat hero <Sequence> layers
data/script.ts: beats [{ startFrame, endFrame, hud:{n,label}, words:[{text,frame,accent?}], hero, extras }] built from the timeline above (multiply seconds by 30)
components/: one file per entry in `components`

Persistent shared objects (DatabaseStack3D, PhoneShopMock, DocumentStack, ReleasePackage/v2, LiveEnvironmentCard) live in a persistent layer with keyframed position/scale so they relocate between beats
rules: Use useCurrentFrame/useVideoConfig/spring/interpolate only - no CSS transitions, setTimeout, requestAnimationFrame or Math.random()
Seed any particles/sparkles by index hash
Fonts via @remotion/google-fonts: Inter, Instrument Serif (italic), JetBrains Mono
Blur-swap captions with interpolate-driven CSS filter: blur()
3D look via layered gradients, inner highlights and multi-layer shadows (no raster images); extruded numerals via stacked offset text-shadows
Audio: <Audio src={staticFile('voice.mp3')} /> and derive word frames from a transcript JSON if available
